report_name: Microsoft & Partners Disrupt Major Phishing-as-a-Service Operation

threat_actors.name: Storm-3119
threat_actors.description: Microsoft-tracked threat actor operating the YAM Store, a Chinese-language Phishing-as-a-Service (PhaaS) marketplace that sold compromised cloud environments for hosting malicious content.

threat_actors.name: Storm-2990
threat_actors.description: Microsoft-tracked threat actor responsible for developing and operating the Iron Man System phishing kit as part of a major Chinese-language PhaaS ecosystem.

threat_actors.name: CoGUI operators
threat_actors.description: The unnamed operators of the CoGUI phishing kit, which was part of a disrupted Chinese-language Phishing-as-a-Service (PhaaS) ecosystem.

attack_patterns.name: Acquire Infrastructure
attack_patterns.description: The YAM Store operators acquired and sold compromised Microsoft and Google cloud environments, providing ready-to-use infrastructure for phishing campaigns.

attack_patterns.name: Domains
attack_patterns.description: The PhaaS operators registered and managed a vast network of domains to host their phishing kits and landing pages.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: The core service of the PhaaS marketplace was enabling the creation and distribution of malicious links designed to steal credentials.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
attack_patterns.description: The PhaaS operators utilized device-code phishing techniques to steal authentication tokens and session cookies, bypassing some forms of multi-factor authentication.

attack_patterns.name: Web Service
attack_patterns.description: The threat actors abused legitimate services like SharePoint and OneDrive to host malicious content and evade detection.

malware.name: CoGUI
malware.description: A phishing kit that provided thousands of phishing templates mimicking legitimate login pages for popular services, sold as part of a Chinese-language PhaaS marketplace.

malware.name: Iron Man System
malware.description: A phishing kit, associated with threat actor Storm-2990, that provided phishing templates and was sold as part of a Chinese-language PhaaS marketplace.

identities.name: Healthcare organizations
identities.description: The healthcare sector was a significant target for phishing campaigns enabled by the YAM Store, CoGUI, and Iron Man PhaaS ecosystem.

identities.name: Financial services organizations
identities.description: The financial services industry was a significant target for phishing campaigns enabled by the YAM Store, CoGUI, and Iron Man PhaaS ecosystem.

infrastructure.name: YAM Store Marketplace
infrastructure.description: A central marketplace operated by Storm-3119 that sold compromised Microsoft and Google environments for hosting phishing content.

infrastructure.name: CoGUI Phishing Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Infrastructure used to host and operate the CoGUI phishing kits as part of a PhaaS marketplace.

infrastructure.name: Iron Man Phishing Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Infrastructure used to host and operate the Iron Man System phishing kits as part of a PhaaS marketplace.

indicators.name: Azure AD Device-Code Phishing Attempt
indicators.pattern:
title: Azure AD Device-Code Phishing Attempt
id: 2a9b4c1d-8e7f-4a3b-9c8d-1e2f3a4b5c6d
status: experimental
description: Detects Azure AD sign-in events using the device_code grant type, which is rare for most users and was abused by the PhaaS operators to bypass MFA.
references:
  - https://www.aha.org/news/headline/2026-10-16-microsoft-health-isac-announce-disruption-cybercriminal-businesses-supplying-attacks-healthcare-others
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
  - attack.t1539
level: medium
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    keywords:
      - 'urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects Azure AD sign-in logs for an increase in `device_code` grant types. Legitimate use is rare for most users. This technique was used by the PhaaS operators to steal authentication tokens.

indicators.name: Anomalous External Sharing from SharePoint
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous External Sharing from SharePoint
id: 3b8c5d2e-9f6a-4b2c-8d7e-2f1a3b4c5d6e
status: experimental
description: 'Detects when a file is shared with an external guest user from SharePoint, which was a technique used by the PhaaS operators to host malicious content.'
references:
  - https://www.aha.org/news/headline/2026-10-16-microsoft-health-isac-announce-disruption-cybercriminal-businesses-supplying-attacks-healthcare-others
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-17
tags:
  - attack.t1102
level: low
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: audit.sharepoint
detection:
  selection:
    Operation: 'FileShared'
    Parameters.TargetUserOrGroupType: 'Guest'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Monitors for anomalous external sharing of files from SharePoint and OneDrive, as these services were abused by the threat actors to host malicious content.
